newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha softens amid poor local demand.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha softens amid poor local demand.

text.p: NWE naphtha softened on Thursday as healthy supply coupled with relaxed end-user demand pressured prices lower, traders said.
Some traders hinted that the market was also being pushed lower by players wanting to ensure the current arbitrage door to Asia remains open.
"I heard one trader is sitting on the market to keep the East-West spread wide," said one trader.
Singapore traders said first-half May open-spec/April NWE spread has widened to around $32 per tonne against $23 two weeks ago.
April swaps were talked around the $204/$206 cif NWE level and May swaps were priced roughly $3 below there.
Traders said a pipeline spec cargo offered out of Grangemouth remained unsold and some players said the seller may have put the cargo into storage. It was supposed to have loaded on Friday.
The seller has offered the cargo in the $200-$202 range over the past few days but bids have failed to breach the $200 mark.
Russian material was heard offered at $198 cif NWE and bid at $194.
Traders said prices for whole-range naphtha cargoes would now come in somewhere around the $197/$199 cif NWE level. -- London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714.
